verdicts.flaw_description: Outcome coverage is restricted to a self-selected subgroup: "The counts cover the sessions that reached the new page, and a quarter of each segment dropped out before checkout." Purchases are counted only among sessions that got as far as the new checkout page, while a quarter of each segment is dropped. Those excluded sessions are exactly the ones least likely to buy, and the comparison baseline (the same segment a month earlier) is not stated to be filtered the same way, so the 4-7 percent lift can be produced by the exclusion rather than by the new page. Everything else in the report is sound (prices held to the cent and every segment browsed the same catalogue).

The measured runs are a filtered subset: "The figures cover the runs with the upgraded filter in service, and a quarter of each stack's runs were made with the filter bypassed." A quarter of runs are excluded from the post-upgrade figures while the comparison is to the same unit a whole quarter earlier, which was not similarly filtered. Bypass runs are plausibly the dirtiest ones, so the 8-14 percent drop can come from dropping them rather than from the filter. The throughput confounder is neutralised (fixed duty cycle, same hours whatever the throughput), so the coverage gap is the live defect.

Classic per-protocol / adherer selection: "Averages cover the patients who kept up the home exercises, and a quarter of each intake let the home exercises lapse." The reported abduction gains are computed only on the compliant three-quarters of each intake, with the non-adherent quarter dropped. Patients who keep up home exercises differ systematically (motivation, less pain, milder injury), so the 9-16 degree gain over the prior quarter may reflect who was kept in the average rather than the protocol itself. The corticosteroid confounder is properly controlled, so this exclusion is the defect.

Germination is scored on a hand-picked subset of trays: "Rates cover the trays sown from seed that took a full coat, and about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed." A fifth of trays are excluded from the post-coating figures, while the comparison (the previous spring sowing) covers everything. Seed that takes a full coat is plausibly the better-formed, more viable seed, so the 6-11 point gain can be an artefact of the exclusion. The temperature confounder is genuinely neutralised (sealed cabinets each at their own set temperature), so the coverage restriction is the failure.

Defect rates are computed on only the fully-treated boards: "Rates cover the boards soldered on the new profile throughout, and about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile." A tenth of each run is dropped from the post-change rate while the month-earlier baseline includes all boards, and the excluded mixed-profile boards are the ones most likely to have been reworked or to have defects. A 6 percent drop in defect rate is small enough that removing a tenth of boards could account for it. The optical-threshold confounder is properly ruled out, so the exclusion is the defect.
